q: How does a sustainability-linked bond coupon step-up work if a target is missed?
title: SLB coupon step-up when a target is missed
short: If the issuer misses its sustainability performance target on the observation date, the bond's coupon rises by a fixed margin, often quoted in basis points, from the next coupon period, usually until maturity. The money raised can be used for any purpose; the penalty is the only link to the target.

ul: KPI: one or more metrics core to the business, such as Scope 1 and 2 tonnes or tonnes CO2 per tonne of product, with a stated baseline year.
Sustainability performance target (SPT): the level the KPI must reach, and the observation date on which it is tested.
Trigger event: the SPT is not met on the observation date, or the KPI is not reported and verified in time.
Step-up: the coupon increase, its size, and the coupon period from which it applies.
Verification: an independent reviewer checks KPI performance; the ICMA Sustainability-Linked Bond Principles call for this at least once a year and for any date that can change the bond's terms.

sections.h: When the higher coupon starts and stops
p: The bond documents fix this, so read the term sheet. A common pattern is: the KPI is measured for a financial year, the verified result is published some months later, and the step-up applies from the first coupon period after that publication date to maturity. The step-up does not normally reverse if the issuer later catches up, unless the documents say so.
Some structures use a one-off premium payment at maturity or a higher redemption price instead of a coupon change. The principle is the same: missing the target costs the issuer money.

sections.h: What SEBI requires for Indian issues
p: SEBI's circular of 5 June 2025 set a framework for ESG debt securities other than green debt securities, covering social, sustainability and sustainability-linked bonds issued under the NCS Regulations. For sustainability-linked bonds the offer document must set out the KPIs, the targets and their rationale, and an independent third-party reviewer assesses them. Labels are expected to follow recognised standards such as the ICMA principles.

sections.h: Checks before you sign up to a target
ol: Can you measure the KPI every year from records an outside reviewer will accept, such as fuel invoices and electricity bills?
Is the baseline fixed, with a rule for recalculating it after an acquisition or a methodology change?
Is the target ambitious beyond business as usual? A soft target draws criticism and may fail the reviewer's assessment.
Have you modelled the cost of missing it over the remaining life of the bond?
What happens if data is late: most documents treat a missing verified report as a missed target.

example.title: Illustrative example: a 25 basis point step-up
lines: Principal: Rs 500 crore, coupon 8.00 percent a year, five years to maturity (figures assumed for illustration)
Target missed; step-up of 25 basis points applies for the last three years
Extra interest each year: 500 crore x 0.25 percent = Rs 1.25 crore
Extra interest over three years: 1.25 x 3 = Rs 3.75 crore, with the coupon now 8.25 percent
example.note: The 25 basis point size is an assumption for illustration; the actual step-up is set in each bond's documents.

senseible: Senseible does not structure, review or verify bonds. It keeps an invoice-backed record of Scope 1 and 2 emissions, with the factor and source on each line, that an issuer can use to track an emissions KPI during the year.
